data.note: Paper Appendix 9.10.2: 1024 series observed at intervals of 0.025 from time 0 to 1, normalized per dimension, corrupted by Gaussian noise std 0.01. Data are regenerated here from the ground-truth SDE with Euler-Maruyama at dt_sim (the paper does not publish the generated dataset itself).

distillation.oracle_diagnostic: the same SINDy procedure fitted to ground-truth field values at the same query states (diagnostic ceiling only, not a candidate)
distillation.query_states: observed states of each split (trajectory-disjoint train/validation/test), teacher evaluated directly (no finite differences)
distillation.selection: per field, minimize validation NRMSE against the teacher; test evaluated once after selection

ground_truth_sde.form: dX = sigma*(Y-X) dt + alpha_x dW1; dY = (X*(rho-Z)-Y) dt + alpha_y dW2; dZ = (X*Y-beta*Z) dt + alpha_z dW3 (diagonal, constant diffusion)

paper.authors: Xuechen Li, Ting-Kam Leonard Wong, Ricky T. Q. Chen, David Duvenaud
paper.experiment: Section 7.2 / Appendix 9.10.2: latent SDE fit to a 3D stochastic Lorenz attractor process
paper.title: Scalable Gradients for Stochastic Differential Equations

simulation.initial_states: test trajectories' observed states at t=0

teacher.architecture: drift MLP and diffusion MLP, each Linear(3,64)-Softplus-Linear(64,64)-Softplus-Linear(64,3); diffusion output Softplus + 0.01 floor; inputs standardized with train-state mean/std
teacher.deviation_from_paper: The paper fits a latent SDE (4-dim latent, GRU encoder, linear decoder, ELBO, stochastic adjoint). Its latent coordinates are not identifiable, so a symbolic equation in latent coordinates could not be compared with the Lorenz SDE. This study therefore estimates a neural SDE directly in the observed 3D state coordinates: drift and diffusion are separate MLPs trained by the Gaussian Euler-Maruyama transition likelihood of the observed trajectories. This is a declared scope cut, not the paper's model.
teacher.loss: mean Gaussian NLL of one-step transitions; v2 variance = g(x)^2*dt_obs + 2*obs_noise_std^2 + (dt_obs^3/3)*sum_j (df_i/dx_j)^2 g_j^2; v1 variance = g(x)^2*dt_obs + 2*obs_noise_std^2
teacher.optimizer: Adam lr 0.002, batch 8192 transitions, 600 epochs, checkpoint = min validation NLL
teacher.estimator: v3 local_linearization_exp (the distilled teacher): local-linearization Gaussian transition likelihood with the mean resummed through the matrix exponential, mean_step = Psi @ f with Psi = integral_0^dt exp(A s) ds from the augmented matrix exponential (A = drift Jacobian, treated as a fixed local coefficient per step), and variance = kappa_i * g_i^2 + (dt^3/3) * sum_{j != i} A_ij^2 g_j^2 + 2*obs_noise_std^2 with kappa_i the diagonal Van Loan factor (exp(2 A_ii dt) - 1) / (2 A_ii). Baselines trained and reported in the estimator comparison: v1 em (plain Euler-Maruyama transition likelihood) and v2 local_linearization (dt^2-truncated mean/variance corrections). Reason for the corrections: at the paper's observation interval dt=0.025 the plain EM likelihood is biased for the nonlinear Lorenz drift - it attributes drift curvature within the interval to the diffusion (v1: g means [0.155, 0.544, 0.507] vs the first, linear component recovered correctly). Estimator revision was decided from this known bias structure and the v1/v2 comparison, before any symbolic model was selected; symbolic selection remained validation-only.
